body:
Let me elaborate on this.

There are two situations: 
1.  The server accepts the connection and after the client and server are connected I kill the client (CTRL-C).
   This leads to an exception in Netty after a few seconds when the underlying UDT socket detects that it does no longer receive heartbeat messages from the client. This is OK because now I can close the connection and cleanup.
2.  The server accepts the connection and after the client and server are connected I let the client disconnect and shutdown gracefully closing the connection properly. I see that the underlying UDT socket is no longer there because both parties (client and server) have stopped sending heartbeat messages to one another. 
   This leads to the situation where the server thinks the channel is still active because there is no notification, and obviously the underlying UDT implementation knows because it has stopped sending heartbeat messages.   

I can workaround this problem by implementing my own heartbeat mechanism on top of the UDT connection, but as this is already implemented by UDT I rather not implement this a second time in the application and should in my opinion be solved lower where the underlying stream is closed.

I hope this helps.

@siteware What you are talking about seems like that ,you connected the client udt channel to the server side,but after you close the client channel ,the server side don't stop?
I don't think this would be an probleam ,cause it server side.you could using the rendezvous instead.

Using rendez-vous is not an option in my case. 

What I expect is that my server handler's method: channelInactive(ChannelHandlerContext ctx) gets called when the client disconnects, this is not the case now.
@siteware the current implement can't match your case

I don't understand, could you please explain your point of view.
Why do you think this is wanted behavior and not a BUG?

I'm just trying to convey that using UDT should be like using TCP sockets as conceptually they are the same.
A disconnection from a client should lead to closing the server side Channel. If you take the UDT C++ implementation, it works the same way, why should this not be reflected in Netty?

@siteware you could have an look at the https://github.com/barchart/barchart-udt project.I am going to porting this to android now,there must be some bugs,but you could take it and then send an pull request.

@Andrei-Pozolotin said that we could send an specified message to the server side ,tell it to close the connection.this is not an TCP just an TCP like.
@siteware, it does seem like a defect in Netty.  I wanted to reproduce it by myself, but it seems like barchart-udt stopped working after upgrading to the latest JDK.

I think it's related to https://github.com/barchart/barchart-udt/pull/49
